The '''Forster–Swan theorem''' is a result from [[commutative algebra]] that states an upper bound for the minimal number of [[Generator (mathematics)|generators]] of a [[finitely generated module]] <math>M</math> over a commutative [[Noetherian ring]]. The usefulness of the theorem stems from the fact, that in order to form the bound, one only needs the minimum number of generators of all [[Localization (commutative algebra)|localizations]] <math>M_{\mathfrak{p}}</math>.

The theorem was proven in a more restrictive form in 1964 by [[Otto Forster]]<ref>{{cite journal |first=Otto |last=Forster |title=Über die Anzahl der Erzeugenden eines Ideals in einem Noetherschen Ring|journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |volume=84|pages=80–87 |date=1964 |doi=10.1007/BF01112211}}</ref> and then in 1967 generalized by [[Richard Swan|Richard G. Swan]]<ref>{{cite journal |first=Richard G. |last=Swan |title=The number of generators of a module |journal=Math. Mathematische Zeitschrift |volume=102 |date=1967 |issue=4 |pages=318–322 |doi=10.1007/BF01110912 |url=https://eudml.org/doc/170878|url-access=subscription }}</ref> to its modern form.

== Forster–Swan theorem==
Let
*<math>R</math> be a commutative Noetherian ring with one,
*<math>M</math> be a finitely generated <math>R</math>-module,
*<math>\mathfrak{p}</math> a [[prime ideal]] of <math>R</math>.
*<math>\mu(M)</math> and <math>\mu_{\mathfrak{p}}(M)</math> are the minimal number of generators needed to generate the <math>R</math>-module <math>M</math> and the <math>R_{\mathfrak{p}}</math>-module <math>M_{\mathfrak{p}}</math>, respectively.

According to [[Nakayama's lemma]], in order to compute <math>\mu_{\mathfrak{p}}(M)</math> one can compute the dimension of <math>M_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}M</math> over the field <math>k(\mathfrak{p})=R_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}R_{\mathfrak{p}}</math>, i.e.
:<math>\mu_{\mathfrak{p}}(M)=\operatorname{dim}_{k(\mathfrak{p})}(M_{\mathfrak{p}}/\mathfrak{p}M).</math>

=== Statement ===
Define the local <math>\mathfrak{p}</math>-bound
:<math>b_{\mathfrak{p}}(M):=\mu_{\mathfrak{p}}(M)+\operatorname{dim}(R/\mathfrak{p}),</math>
then the following holds<ref>{{citation|author=R. A. Rao und F. Ischebeck |date=2005 |editor=Physica-Verlag |location=Deutschland |pages=221 |title=Ideals and Reality: Projective Modules and Number of Generators of Ideals}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
:<math>\mu(M)\leq \sup_{\mathfrak{p}}\;\{b_{\mathfrak{p}}(M)\;|\;\mathfrak{p}\;\text{is prime},\;M_{\mathfrak{p}}\neq 0\}.</math>
